phase: fixed before new issue title scoring, assertions and browser runs
normalizedMargin: (first-second)/first; if first==0 record null and exclude no lexical evidence
query: Original public issue title, verbatim. Score every action except ordinary with the project's original BM25.
population: Bounded convenience sample from the three fixed upstreams in the declared order. For vanilla, take GitHub issue references from the official npm release's CHANGELOG. For Swiper take issues explicitly closed or fixed in the bug-fix sections of the official CHANGELOG at v11.2.10. For flatpickr take issue references from GitHub release notes of v4.6.13 and older 4.6.x releases. Traverse newest release first, in source order within release. Take up to 18 distinct referenced numbers per library in the initial wave. If fewer than two can be qualified, permit one further wave of the next 18 per library. Keep all screened rows, including duplicates with historical work, PRs, non-UI items and unavailable metadata. Do not retrieve security-related reports.
eligibility: Closed, new, ordinary UI issue with positive first lexical score and margin <= threshold. Consider eligible rows in round-robin source order across libraries. Stop after two qualified independent tickets. Keep candidates not attempted in the ledger. Require published buggy and repaired builds, meaningful replay with the immutable action families, passing ordinary action, all reference controls passing and at least one candidate-specific failure confirmed on repeat. Record all failing actions; do not select by target text position or by policy outcome.
construction: Reuse original menu descriptions verbatim and original array order for lexical ties. Vanilla uses the same date menu except time, which its date-only UI does not implement. Give each menu family one executable scenario per ticket. Apply the public UI case configuration to the relevant family and use ordinary working examples for the remaining families. Freeze executable scenarios, common oracle and build identities before candidate execution. Explicitly identify fixtures adapted during qualification.
policies: Smoke first. BM25 orders the full menu. Both strategies share the same top three candidates. For each candidate use a fresh page and execute the action once on the reference version. Decode the raw pre/post pair of the fixed local window, compute normalized mean absolute RGB change. Rank by descending change (average tied ranks), add BM25 rank, break ties by original BM25 order. Zero uses the same ranker with all deltas zero. All three orders are locked before candidate assertions. Each strategy executes at most three candidate actions total and stops on its first failure. Complete independent acceptance covers the full menu and is accounted separately.
